title: High prices strain budgets of small business owner and single mom in Virginia's 1st district
content: Small business owners and single mothers in rural Virginia’s 1st Congressional District are facing financial strain due to high prices. These residents describe how they are managing the economic stress of the current period.
summary: High prices are straining the budgets of a small business owner and a single mother in a rural part of Virginia's 1st Congressional district. They explain how they're handling the economic stress of these times.
author: NPR Politics

title: Red Hill, Colorado residents oppose drone‑sprayed weed‑killer plan
content:
Officials in Red Hill, Colorado, have outlined a plan to use drones to spray weed‑killing chemicals over the area in an effort to eradicate invasive weeds. The proposal, described by the officials as safe, is set to begin soon in the Red Hill portion of Boulder County. 

Some local residents have voiced opposition, saying they are concerned about the chemicals being dispersed from the sky onto a wildland noted for its biodiversity, hundreds of important species, rare environmental resources, and as a key habitat for elk and bighorn sheep, with farms and ranchland at its base.
summary: Officials in Red Hill, Colorado say a drone program will safely spray weed‑killing chemicals to eliminate invasive weeds. Some local residents object, noting the aerial applications will fall over a biodiverse wildland that supports elk, bighorn sheep and nearby farms and ranches.
author: Guardian Environment

title: MD Anderson discovers pathway that drives KRAS protein production in common cancers
content: New research from The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center has identified a previously unknown mechanism that enables cancer cells to selectively produce tumor‑driving proteins such as KRAS in common cancers. The study suggests that inhibiting a particular enzyme involved in this pathway could enhance the effectiveness of targeted therapies and may help overcome treatment resistance.
summary: Researchers at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center identified a previously unknown mechanism that enables cancer cells to selectively produce tumor‑growth proteins such as KRAS. They say that targeting the enzyme involved in this pathway could improve responses to targeted therapies and help overcome treatment resistance.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Clot removal after stroke may aid recovery but carries risks
content:
After a stroke, doctors treat time as a critical factor. Each minute that blood cannot reach the brain raises the risk of permanent damage or death.  

Endovascular thrombectomy offers a way to restore circulation. The minimally invasive procedure physically removes the clot, reestablishes blood flow, and can markedly lower the risk of long‑term disability or death.  

Because of its effectiveness, mechanical thrombectomy is the standard emergency treatment for acute ischemic stroke within the first 24 hours after the event.
summary: After a stroke, each minute of blocked blood flow increases the risk of permanent brain damage. Endovascular thrombectomy, a minimally invasive clot‑removal procedure, can restore circulation and lower the chance of long‑term disability or death and is a standard emergency treatment within the first 24 hours of an acute ischemic stroke.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Trump administration proposes cash for married parents to stay home, experts question adequacy
content:
The Trump administration has proposed a program that would provide financial assistance to married parents who choose to stay at home. Experts say the plan emphasizes “traditional families” and does not account for the broader flexibility many households need to support themselves.

Erica Hall’s experience illustrates those concerns. She and her husband spaced their children five years apart to avoid the cost of two daycare spots, self‑funded her first maternity leave with savings, and was recently laid off from her tech job, leaving her uncertain about how to manage childcare expenses.
summary: The Trump administration has proposed a program that would give married parents money to stay at home. Experts say the proposal favors traditional families and may not provide enough flexibility for all families, as illustrated by Erica Hall’s experience with costly childcare and a recent job loss.
author: Guardian Business

title: Affordability dominates voter concerns ahead of Tuesday midterms as Ohio strike nears record
content:
Affordability is a leading concern for voters as they head to the polls on Tuesday, with many saying they must choose between medicine and groceries. The cost‑of‑living pressure has dominated this election cycle, prompting workers and unions to back candidates who promise higher wages and measures to curb rising prices.

In Lorain County, Ohio, the issue is reflected locally: Gina Jones and her co‑workers at Lorain County Job and Family Services have been on strike since February 2026. The walkout is the longest public‑sector strike in Ohio’s history and could become the longest on record in the United States.
summary: Affordability dominates voter concerns ahead of Tuesday midterms as Ohio strike nears record.
author: Guardian Business

title: Researchers realize anti-spin ice that breaks ice rule, Nature Communications reports
content: Scientists have employed attracting particles to construct an “anti‑spin ice,” a system that reverses the behavior of conventional spin ices by breaking the ice rule that normally governs them. The achievement was reported in a recent Nature Communications study, which documents the realization of this opposite‑type spin‑ice configuration.
summary: Researchers reported the realization of an anti-spin ice in a recent Nature Communications study. The anti-spin ice system opposes conventional spin ices by breaking the ice rule that governs them.
author: Phys.org

title: 2,700‑year‑old mummy head provides first molecular proof of aloe in Egyptian embalming
content: An interdisciplinary team at Marburg University applied modern natural‑product analysis together with Egyptology and the history of pharmacy to a 2,700‑year‑old mummy head. Their study produced the first molecular evidence that aloe was used in ancient Egyptian embalming.
summary: Researchers identified molecular traces of aloe in a 2,700‑year‑old mummy head, linking the plant to ancient Egyptian embalming. The interdisciplinary team at Marburg University used modern natural product analysis combined with Egyptology and pharmacy history to make the discovery.
author: Phys.org

title: 3I/ATLAS comet's methane rich in heavy hydrogen points to frigid origin
content: The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS contains methane that is unusually rich in heavy hydrogen. This chemical signature indicates that the comet’s frozen material formed in an intensely cold environment, either around another star or in the molecular cloud that preceded it, before the object entered the Solar System.
summary: The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS has a methane signature unusually rich in heavy hydrogen. This suggests its frozen ingredients formed in an intensely cold environment around another star or in the preceding cloud.
author: Phys.org

title: Permanent daylight saving time in parts of Canada could affect schools
content: Adopting permanent daylight‑saving time in British Columbia, the Northwest Territories, Alberta, Manitoba and northwestern Ontario would end the semi‑annual clock changes. Because sleep is fundamental to well‑being, officials note that the shift could disrupt sleep for many Canadians, a change that may affect school schedules and student health.
summary: British Columbia, the Northwest Territories, Alberta, Manitoba and northwestern Ontario have decided to end semiannual clock changes and remain on permanent daylight saving time. The shift could affect schools by causing potential sleep disruption for many Canadians.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists create molecular motor based on Archimedes’ screw that boosts conductivity 100‑fold
content: Scientists have created a molecular motor that mimics the ancient Archimedes’ screw, reducing the device to a single‑molecule scale. The motor can rotate clockwise or counter‑clockwise when powered by electricity, and its motion can increase electrical conductivity by as much as one hundredfold, a development that may influence future molecular‑electronics technologies.
summary: Scientists have built a molecular motor that spins in either direction when powered by electricity and is modeled on the Archimedes’ screw invented more than 2,000 years ago. The motor’s rotation can increase electrical conductivity by up to 100 times, a development that could impact molecular electronics.
author: Science Daily

title: Crown-of-thorns starfish may aid Great Barrier Reef health, study finds
content: Crown‑of‑thorns starfish, long identified as a major threat to coral reefs, may also play a beneficial role when their numbers are controlled, according to new research on Australia’s Great Barrier Reef. Scientists observed that roughly three‑quarters of the starfish’s feeding incidents left living coral tissue intact instead of wiping out whole colonies. By preferentially consuming fast‑growing, dominant corals, the predators open space for slower‑growing species, a process that could boost coral biodiversity on the reef.
summary: Scientists studying the Great Barrier Reef found that about three‑quarters of observed crown‑of‑thorns starfish feeding events left living coral tissue instead of destroying entire colonies. By grazing on fast‑growing dominant corals, the starfish create space for slower‑growing species, potentially increasing coral biodiversity when their populations are kept in check.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds daily peanuts boost brain health and memory in older adults
content: Scientists report that a new study found older adults who ate about two servings of unsalted, skin‑roasted peanuts each day for 16 weeks showed improved insulin responsiveness in brain regions important for memory. The researchers suggest this daily peanut intake could help support brain health and memory, functions that often weaken with age and are linked to Alzheimer’s disease.
summary: Study finds daily peanuts boost brain health and memory in older adults.
author: Science Daily

title: University of Virginia scientists develop ultrasound‑nanoparticle therapy for glioblastoma
content: Scientists at the University of Virginia have created an experimental strategy against glioblastoma, a highly lethal brain cancer. The approach uses focused ultrasound—sound waves—to deliver tiny nanoparticles loaded with microRNAs, enabling simultaneous targeting of several cancer‑driving genes.
summary: Scientists at the University of Virginia have created an experimental strategy to treat glioblastoma, a deadly brain cancer. The approach combines focused ultrasound, tiny nanoparticles and microRNAs to attack multiple cancer-driving genes simultaneously.
author: Science Daily

title: 17‑18‑million‑year‑old Egyptian ape fossil suggests North Africa as ape cradle
content: A 17‑ to 18‑million‑year‑old ape fossil uncovered in Egypt is prompting scientists to reassess the geographic origins of modern apes and humans. The find challenges the traditional view that East Africa was the primary cradle of ape evolution, suggesting instead that North Africa and the Middle East may have played that role.
summary: A 17- to 18-million-year-old ape fossil discovered in Egypt is challenging long-held beliefs about where the ancestors of humans and other modern apes first evolved. Scientists now suspect that North Africa and the Middle East, rather than East Africa, may have been the cradle of modern ape evolution.
author: Science Daily

title: UCLA study links common pesticide to over 2.5‑fold increased Parkinson’s risk
content: A UCLA study reported that long‑term exposure to a common pesticide is associated with more than 2.5 times higher risk of Parkinson’s disease. The researchers also described the mechanism by which the chemical harms brain cells and highlighted a promising approach to protect those cells.
summary: A UCLA study found that long‑term exposure to a common pesticide was linked to more than 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson’s disease. The researchers also described how the chemical damages brain cells and reported a promising method to protect them.
author: Science Daily

title: Study of 486,000 adults links 6‑8 cups of tea daily to 11% lower heart disease risk
content: A study of almost 486,000 adults found that regular tea consumption was linked to an 11 % lower risk of heart and blood‑vessel disease. The greatest risk reduction was observed among participants who drank roughly six to eight cups daily, with black tea showing more consistent benefits than green tea.
summary: A study of nearly 486,000 adults found that regular tea drinking was associated with an 11% lower risk of heart and blood vessel diseases. The lowest risk was observed among those who drank about six to eight cups per day, with black tea showing more consistent benefits than green tea.
author: Science Daily

title: UK cannabis market booms but artist Louis Petit lacks epilepsy treatment
content:
The UK’s legal cannabis market is expanding, yet patients with serious illnesses remain unable to obtain NHS prescriptions for the drug. Companies have rushed to supply cannabis as a wellness treatment, but the NHS has not provided prescriptions for those who need it for medical conditions.

Louis Petit, a prodigiously talented young artist, illustrates the gap. Diagnosed at age 12 with a rare neurological disease in 2016, he was forced to leave the UK for the Netherlands, where medical cannabis was legal. In Rotterdam, doctors prescribed a cannabis oil called Bedrolite alongside anti‑epileptic medication, a combination that slowed and eventually stopped his seizures—something his UK neurologists had previously deemed impossible.

Dr Kojo Koram, a professor of law and political economy at Loughborough University and author of The Next Fix: The Winners and Losers in the Future of Drugs, highlights the contrast between the booming market and the lack of access for patients like Petit.
summary: UK cannabis market booms but artist Louis Petit lacks epilepsy treatment.
author: Guardian Science

title: OmniDiff: Open-source Rust Git difftool handles code, images, PDFs, runs under 100 ms
content: I have been researching what the ultimate diff tool would look like, based on actual diffs in open source repositories. OmniDiff can diff: code (25 languages), config, images, PDFs, archives, cursors, fonts... It's fast. It can diff C++ files of tens of thousands of lines in under 100ms, on a 2023 ThinkPad T14s. It's open source. AGPLv3. It's based on real diffs. I looked at the 7400 repositories that are listed in Gentoo packages, sampled 2000 diffs and solved them manually to get a good understanding of what is needed, before putting together the diff pipelines for each content type. Incidentally, this also forms the basis of the CI pipeline, so the robustness of the codebase is quite high. I'm still developing it. It's v0.3.0 at this time. But I have been using it daily as my git difftool for months now, and it works well. AI Disclosure: Yes, I do use AI. No, I do not vibecode. Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50325253 Points: 4 # Comments: 7
summary: OmniDiff: Open-source Rust Git difftool handles code, images, PDFs, runs under 100 ms.
author: Hacker News

title: Anti‑data‑center candidates poised to win Tuesday amid New York moratorium
content: On Tuesday, several anti‑data‑center candidates are poised to win in New York, providing a glimpse of the tensions the state faces over how to address its digital‑infrastructure needs. The upcoming results underscore the challenges of taking concrete action on this issue.
summary: A number of anti-data-center candidates are poised to win on Tuesday. The race highlights tensions in New York over how to address digital infrastructure.
author: Wired

title: Lenovo LOQ 15 named only gaming laptop under $1,500 worth buying
content: The article notes that, amid rising prices for gaming laptops, the Lenovo LOQ 15 remains the sole affordable option under $1,500. It is described as delivering better performance and a superior display than competing models.
summary: Prices for gaming laptops are escalating. The Lenovo LOQ 15 is the sole affordable option, offering better performance and display than its competitors.
author: Wired

title: California Prop 45 could give data center developers a loophole to avoid scrutiny
content:
A California ballot initiative, Proposition 45, proposes to accelerate the review process for projects deemed “essential” infrastructure. The measure would shorten state‑mandated environmental assessment timelines for qualifying projects and raise the bar for residents seeking to challenge those projects in court. Proponents argue the faster approvals would ease the state’s housing shortage and support new renewable‑energy projects needed to meet rising electricity demand.  

Environmental advocates and some legal experts caution that the measure could create a loophole allowing data‑center developers to avoid public scrutiny, noting the backing of data‑center interests for the proposal.
summary: Proposition 45 would shorten timelines for state‑mandated environmental assessments for eligible projects and make it more difficult for residents to challenge those projects in court. Environmental groups and some legal experts warn the measure could give data center developers a loophole to evade public scrutiny.
author: The Verge

title: GTA VI and new Zelda game slated for November 2026 as top releases
content:
The Stepback is a weekly newsletter that breaks down one essential story from the tech world. It is delivered to subscribers’ inboxes every Sunday at 8 AM ET, and readers can opt in through a link provided in the newsletter. For additional coverage of the year’s biggest game releases, the newsletter recommends following Andrew Webster.

The newsletter’s “How it started” section notes that the two biggest games of 2026 will launch a few weeks apart in November. One of those titles is Grand Theft Auto VI, described as a 13‑year‑old experience and the sequel to one of the best‑selling games ever. Its predecessor, GTA V, has sold 230 million copies since its 2013 launch and was re‑released.
summary: The two biggest games of 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI and a new Zelda title, are scheduled to launch within weeks of each other in November. GTA VI follows GTA V, which has sold 230 million copies since its 2013 release.
author: The Verge

title: Apple's HomePod Mini 2: Nice Upgrade but No Major Improvements Yet
content:
Apple’s second‑generation HomePod Mini, priced at $149, arrives as a modest upgrade over the original $99 model. The new speaker includes a chip bump, subtle color changes, and improved AirPlay support, but its sound system remains unchanged from the first‑generation version.

Initially, the reviewer expressed disappointment, noting that a $50 price increase had not delivered a significant audio upgrade. Despite this, hands‑on testing in a home office setting has shifted the reviewer’s view.

The Mini 2 demonstrates noticeably faster performance, playing music within seconds and responding to smart‑home commands more quickly than its predecessor. The overall experience, while still lacking a major sound improvement, feels more responsive and polished.
summary: Apple released the second-generation HomePod Mini priced at $149, a $50 increase over the original $99 model. The new speaker offers a chip bump, color glowy effects, and improved AirPlay, but its sound system remains unchanged.
author: The Verge

title: Keeping your birthday private can help prevent identity theft
content:
Using a fake date of birth—or leaving that field blank—when creating an online account can help protect against identity theft, according to the article. The piece warns that sharing your birthdate can enable fraudsters to verify their false identities.

It illustrates the risk with a scenario in which a caller claims to be from a bank, reads out the victim’s name, address and date of birth, and thereby convinces the person the call is legitimate. In reality, the criminals have already obtained the birthday and are using it to impersonate the account holder.
summary: Using a fake date of birth or leaving the field blank when creating an online account can provide protection from identity theft. Criminals can use a person’s date of birth as verification information to impersonate them, as illustrated by a bank‑call scenario.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Iran's supreme leader warns of geographically unrestricted response to any US attack
content: Iran’s supreme leader warned of a "geographically unrestricted response" if the United States attacks again. As Iran ramps up threats without excluding pre-emptive military action, its officials noted positive steps in mediated negotiations with the US ahead of the decisive midterm elections. Meanwhile, Gulf countries remain braced for the worst.
summary: Iran’s supreme leader warned of a geographically unrestricted response if the United States attacks again and said Tehran does not exclude pre‑emptive military action. Iranian officials said there are positive steps in mediated negotiations with the United States, while Gulf countries said they remain braced for the worst.
author: Euronews

title: Flags, banners and chants at youth protest in Berlin
content:
Hundreds of young demonstrators gathered outside Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate.  
The “GenZ regelt!” movement called for nationwide protests against political and social issues, in solidarity with student demonstrations across Europe.
summary: Hundreds of young demonstrators gathered outside Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate as the “GenZ regelt!” movement called for nationwide protests against political and social issues, in solidarity with student demonstrations across Europe.
author: Euronews

title: Heidi Klum dresses as giant severed hand at 25th annual Halloween party
content: Celebrities convened in New York for Heidi Klum’s 25th annual Halloween party, where the host presented herself as a giant, gruesome severed hand. Attendees complemented the theme by arriving in a variety of elaborate costumes.
summary: Heidi Klum hosted her 25th annual Halloween party in New York, where celebrities attended. The host dressed as a giant severed hand while guests arrived in elaborate costumes.
author: Euronews

title: Riots and looting erupt in Frankfurt after youth demonstrations, police stay
content: Police stayed on the streets of Frankfurt on Sunday after rioting and looting erupted following youth demonstrations. The unrest left shopfronts smashed, fires burning and several people injured.
summary: Police stayed on the streets of Frankfurt on Sunday after rioting and looting erupted following youth demonstrations. The unrest left shopfronts smashed, fires burning and several people injured.
author: Euronews

title: Swiss foreign minister visits North Korea for first time since 2003 as office reopens
content: Switzerland’s foreign minister has travelled to North Korea, marking the first visit by a Swiss official since 2003, as the country reopens its diplomatic office in Pyongyang. The move is part of Switzerland’s effort to renew direct talks with North Korea amid rising tensions on the peninsula, and Seoul hopes the Swiss presence will facilitate its own engagement with Pyongyang.
summary: The Swiss foreign minister visited North Korea, marking the first such visit since 2003 as the Swiss diplomatic office reopened. Switzerland is renewing direct talks with North Korea, and Seoul hopes the Swiss office will help it engage with Pyongyang.
author: Euronews

title: Youth Olympic Games open in Senegal, first Olympic competition in Africa
content:
Senegal marked a historic moment on Saturday as the Youth Olympic Games began in the Dakar region, becoming the first Olympic competition held on African soil. An opening ceremony drew about 30,000 spectators.

The Games will feature 2,700 athletes aged 14 to 17 competing in 25 sports across three Senegalese cities.
summary: The Youth Olympic Games officially began in Senegal's Dakar region on Saturday with an opening ceremony attended by 30,000 people. The event features 2,700 athletes aged 14 to 17 competing in 25 sports across three Senegalese cities.
author: France 24

title: Lula wins Brazil reelection, Israel election razor‑sharp margins, Spain train crash kills
content: From Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection in Brazil's presidential polls, to razor-sharp margins in the Israeli general elections, to a deadly high-speed train collision in Spain, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.
summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva was reelected in Brazil's presidential polls. Israel's general election was decided by razor‑sharp margins, and a deadly high‑speed train collision in Spain killed people.
author: France 24

title: Route du Rhum fleet set to depart from Saint-Malo for solo transatlantic race
content: The Route du Rhum fleet is ready to depart from Saint‑Malo in Brittany for the solo transatlantic race to Guadeloupe. Billed as the world’s biggest solo transatlantic competition, the event features both professional and amateur skippers and is held every four years, Selina Sykes reports.
summary: The Route du Rhum, billed as the world’s biggest solo transatlantic race, is set to depart from Saint‑Malo in Brittany. Skippers, both professional and amateur, will sail alone to Guadeloupe in the quadrennial event.
author: France 24

title: European Commission urges Poland’s President Nawrocki to recognise Tusk‑appointed judges
content: Poland’s constitutional crisis deepened on Saturday when the European Commission urged President Karol Nawrocki to recognise new judges appointed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The standoff comes ahead of next year’s parliamentary election, with polls indicating a close race between Tusk’s coalition and the nationalist right, reports Camille Corcoran.
summary: Poland’s constitutional crisis deepened on Saturday when the European Commission urged President Karol Nawrocki to recognise new judges appointed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The standoff comes ahead of next year’s parliamentary election, with polls suggesting a close race between Tusk’s coalition and the nationalist right.
author: France 24

title: Democrats confront internal leftward surge ahead of midterms
content: Democrats are aiming to regain control of Congress as internal divisions surface over the party’s direction. A new wave of progressive candidates is urging a shift further to the left, targeting corporate money in politics and advocating universal healthcare, climate action and an end to police violence. Monte Francis reports.
summary: Democrats are seeking to regain control of Congress as internal divisions emerge over the party’s future direction. A new wave of progressive candidates is pushing the party further left, challenging corporate money in politics and advocating universal healthcare, climate action and an end to police violence.
author: France 24

title: French high school blockades set to resume Monday, student unions announce
content: The head of a student union announced on Sunday that high‑school blockades across France will restart on Monday. President Emmanuel Macron has urged that classes resume following the government’s announcement of new measures to address the ongoing education crisis, which student groups said were insufficient.
summary: The head of a student union said Sunday that high school blockades throughout France would restart on Monday. French President Emmanuel Macron called for classes to resume after the government announced new measures to address the education crisis, which student groups found insufficient.
author: France 24

title: Oleshky residents cross into Ukrainian-held area after rare local truce
content:
Residents evacuated from Russian‑occupied Oleshky have reached Ukrainian‑held territory after a rare local truce. The return follows years of isolation and regular shelling in the city.

The evacuees described severe food shortages, saying some were forced to eat grass and dogs to survive. Oleshky was seized by Russian forces in the early days of the 2022 invasion and remains cut off by the Dnipro River on one side and Russian troops on the other.
summary: Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky have reached Ukrainian-held territory following a rare local truce. They described years of isolation, food shortages and regular shelling, with some saying they were forced to eat grass and dogs to survive.
author: France 24

title: John Healey says UK apology for slave trade will not include reparations
content: Ahead of a meeting with Commonwealth leaders, Andy Burnham wrote that Britain needed to ‘acknowledge its complicated history’ At the end of his interview with Kuennsberg, Healey was also asked to comment on a potential apology for Britain’s near-250 years of perpetrating the slave trade and why the government should or shouldn’t pay reparations to enslaved people and their countries. Sitting in the grand settings of Number 11 Downing St, Kuenssberg pointed out the lavish interiors: Considering a formal apology doesn’t mean accepting that British people now should accept the financial liability for any party and things that happened hundreds of years ago, in which they had no role. For almost 250 years (1560s-1807), British ships trafficked more than three million enslaved African men, women and children in a state policy backed by the monarchy and parliament. Many were taken to British-owned plantations in the Caribbean, which enslaved generations. Children were born into slavery, uprisings were put down with extreme brutality There were still 800,000 enslaved people on British plantations when enslavement was finally abolished by parliament in 1833 Abolishment was only achieved because the government agreed to “compensate” the enslavers. The government paid an enormous sum, the equivalent of billions of dollars these days, to the “owners” of enslaved people; this came from a huge loan that was only paid off in 2015. Britain has never paid any compensation or reparations to the people who were enslaved, or their countries. U. K. Politicians have traditionally focused on the country’s role in banning the slave trade in 1807 and outlawing slavery throughout the British Empire in 1833.
summary: John Healey told interviewers that a formal apology for Britain’s historic slave‑trade role would not create financial liability for the British public. He said an apology does not mean the UK should pay reparations to enslaved people or their descendant communities.
author: Guardian World

title: Home Office still flies asylum seekers to France weeks after ‘one in one out’ scheme ended
content:
The Guardian reports that the Home Office continues to detain and remove asylum seekers to France weeks after the “one in, one out” scheme officially ended. The newspaper understands that dozens of individuals remain in detention, with one group forcibly removed from the UK just this week.

The controversial policy was announced in July 2025 by French President Emmanuel Macron and former Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Its goal was to deter small boat crossings from northern France by forcibly returning some asylum seekers to France while legally bringing a similar number of people from the region to the UK.
summary: Home Office still flies asylum seekers to France weeks after ‘one in one out’ scheme ended.
author: Guardian World

title: Cambridge scientist Marta Shahbazi killed in Spain train crash
content:
Tributes have been offered for Dr Marta Shahbazi, described as an “inspiring” University of Cambridge scientist who died in the Spanish train collision on Wednesday that killed at least 69 people.  

Dr Shahbazi was an affiliate associate professor at the Cambridge Stem Cell Institute and a group leader at the Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology in Cambridge. She was travelling to a conference to receive an award for scientific excellence in developmental biology when the train she was on was involved in the crash near Urda in Toledo province.
summary: Cambridge scientist Marta Shahbazi killed in Spain train crash.
author: Guardian World

title: NT government plan to scrap environmental water allocation condemned as shameless attack
content: Exclusive : Move to scrap legal requirement to set aside water for environment is ‘extreme even for the NT CLP government’, green group says Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The Northern Territory government has been accused of making a “blatant and shameless” attack on nature by planning to delete a legal requirement that water must be allocated to the environment. In what has been described as the latest in a series of attacks on the environment by the NT’s Country Liberal party, the Finocchiaro government plans to change water rules that govern how much ground and surface water industry can take.
summary: The Northern Territory government under the Finocchiaro administration intends to delete the legal requirement that water be set aside for the environment. A green group called the move a “blatant and shameless” attack on nature and said it is extreme even for the NT Country Liberal party.
author: Guardian World

title: Former NSW Liberal Mark Jones leads overhaul of One Nation candidate selection
content:
Mark Jones, a former Liberal Party member from New South Wales, is now leading an overhaul of One Nation’s candidate‑selection process. After being one of the final three contenders for the position of state director of the NSW Liberal branch in 2023, his advancement was blocked, according to multiple Liberal sources familiar with the recruitment.  

Three years later, Jones is described as instrumental in One Nation’s expansion, taking a key role in selecting and vetting the party’s candidates who aim to challenge his former Liberal colleagues. The source notes his shift from a prospective senior Liberal role to a central position within One Nation’s electoral strategy.
summary: Mark Jones, who was among the final three candidates for the New South Wales Liberal state director role, is now instrumental in One Nation's expansion. He is leading an effort to select and vet One Nation candidates aimed at beating his former Liberal colleagues.
author: Guardian World

title: Australian home values fall seventh month, fastest in 40 years; Brisbane, Perth lead
content:
Australian home values have fallen for a seventh straight month, with prices in the capital cities declining at the fastest rate in four decades. The slide is linked to rising mortgage rates that are deterring buyers, according to Cotality data.

The centre of the downturn is moving away from Sydney and Melbourne toward mid‑sized state capitals. In October, Brisbane and Perth recorded the steepest declines, although most homeowners remain on sizeable gains after a period of strong growth.
summary: Australian home values have dropped for a seventh consecutive month, with capital‑city prices falling at the fastest pace in 40 years as rising mortgage rates deter buyers. Cotality data shows the downturn’s centre shifting from Sydney and Melbourne toward mid‑sized capitals, with Brisbane and Perth recording the biggest October declines.
author: Guardian World

title: US-China trade war appears subdued but underlying tension persists
content:
A truce has cooled the U.S.–China trade conflict, yet neither nation has taken steps to limit the possibility of new hostilities. The article notes that Donald Trump’s trade wars have largely disappeared from headlines, although occasional fears of fresh tariffs arise when the president makes statements such as threatening to end U.S. trade with deficit‑running countries unless the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates.

While attention has shifted to other concerns—including worries about Trump’s impact on American democracy and speculative threats from artificial intelligence—the piece warns that the apparent calm may be misleading. It argues that, beneath the surface, the world is moving toward an economic war of potentially epic proportions, one that history suggests could eventually spill over into actual conflict.
summary: A truce has cooled the US-China trade conflict, but neither country has taken steps to limit the risk of new hostilities. The apparent calm is misleading, as the world may be moving toward an economic war of potentially epic proportions despite other headline concerns.
author: Guardian World

title: Judge dismisses Trump's lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein birthday book
content: A judge has dismissed former President Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal. The case stemmed from the newspaper’s publication of a letter to Jeffrey Epstein, presented as a birthday‑book contribution that was purportedly written and signed by Trump.
summary: A judge dismissed Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal. The suit concerned the paper's publication of a letter to Epstein that was claimed to have been written and signed by Trump for an Epstein birthday book.
author: BBC World

title: Gabby Williams scores 30 as Golden State Valkyries win first WNBA title in Game 7
content:
The Golden State Valkyries captured their first WNBA championship by defeating the Dream 68‑63 in the league’s inaugural Game 7. Gabby Williams led the victory with 30 points, and the win marked the franchise’s first title in just its second season. The decisive game took place at the Chase Center, where the Valkyries gathered to celebrate the historic achievement.

Following the final buzzer, teammates embraced on the court, with Kaila Charles hugging Tiffany Hayes and Kayla Thornton cheering loudly as the team lifted the trophy.

title: Salford City, backed by Beckham, lead League Two after eighth straight win
content:
Salford City, after seven seasons in League Two, are positioning themselves as a potential challenger for promotion to the Championship. The club’s recent form includes an eighth consecutive victory, a 2‑1 win over Exeter, which leaves them five points clear at the top of the division.

The team’s progress follows a change in ownership that saw Gary Neville and David Beckham join a new consortium in May 2025, adding to the earlier involvement of the Class of ’92 that had guided the club from non‑league football into the fourth tier. An expanded budget has enabled Salford to recruit players deemed above League Two standard, notably striker Macaulay Langstaff from Millwall—who previously scored 28 goals in a season for Notts County at this level—and midfielder Will Aimson, who dropped down from a two‑season spell with Wigan.
summary: Salford City, owned in part by Gary Neville and David Beckham, sit five points clear at the top of League Two after an eighth consecutive victory over Exeter. The club has increased its budget and added striker Macaulay Langstaff from Millwall and defender Will Aimson from Wigan as it targets promotion to the Championship.

title: Jillaroos crush Wales 124-6 in Rugby League World Cup, set record score
content:
The Australian women’s rugby league team, the Jillaroos, defeated Wales 124‑6 in a Pool A match of the Rugby League World Cup. The win featured six tries from Jaime Chapman and served as a warm‑up ahead of the tournament’s semi‑finals.

The 124‑6 result established a new women’s World Cup record for both total points and winning margin, surpassing the previous 92‑0 victory recorded by Australia over France in 2022. It also exceeded the men’s tournament record of 110‑4 set by the Kangaroos against Russia in 2000, despite the women’s game being ten minutes shorter. The Jillaroos’ 124 points represent the highest score ever recorded in an international rugby league match.
summary: Jillaroos crush Wales 124-6 in Rugby League World Cup, set record score.

title: Carrick defiant after latest defeat as Glasner and Le Bris discuss rebuilding

Sunderland head coach Régis Le Bris commented on his team’s demanding schedule, noting that the club is aware of its situation. He explained that clubs entering European competition often experience a reduction of around ten points in their first season, describing this as a realistic expectation for Sunderland.
summary: Carrick said he remained defiant after his side’s latest defeat. Oliver Glasner said he will rebuild Nottingham Forest from the bottom up, while Sunderland head coach Régis Le Bris warned his club faces a demanding schedule and expects fewer points in Europe.

title: Top New Science-Fiction Books Released in November 2026
content: Characters in The Falling, out this month, face a similar danger to those in the film Deep Impact, shown here Paramount/Everett/Shutte​rstock I am currently deeply engrossed in the November read for the New Scientist Book Club, a piece of classic science fiction (well, from 2012) from Chris Beckett, Dark Eden. But I’m also in the mood for some fresh writing, and the new sci-fi on offer this month is an exciting and eclectic range. I’m keen to check out Benjamin Percy’s audio drama Exoplanet, produced by none other than Andy Weir, as well as books from some old favourites: Michael Moorcock, Carole Hailey, John Scalzi and Andrew Hunter Murray. And for all those still in the mood for scares after Halloween, there’s some space horror from SA Barnes in the deliciously named Cold Eternity. The best new science-fiction books of October 2026 Exoplanet by Benjamin Percy This is something a little different – produced by Andy Weir, author of The Martian and Project Hail Mary, and written by Benjamin Percy, this sci-fi thriller is a full-cast audio drama from Audible, and it sounds really exciting. It follows the fallout when a quantum anomaly tears a starship apart, leaving its crew in different eras on the same deadly exoplanet – one in a machine-ruled future, for example, another in a past peopled by hostile aliens. I’m a recent (only this year) audiobook adopter, and this sounds right up my street. Matt Damon in the film adaptation of Andy Weir’s novel The Martian Aidan Monaghan/THA/Shutterstoc​k Everything Happens So Much by Andrew Hunter Murray I really enjoyed Andrew Hunter Murray’s speculative novel The Last Day, in which the world stops turning, leaving half the planet in scorching sunlight and the other half permanently dark. This latest book sounds equally interesting. A young woman, Esme, escapes her dull job by taking tiny potions known as The Elsewheres, which allow her to visit alternate versions of herself. But then an “incident” turns her into the most important person in this, or possibly any, universe. How will she handle it? Advertisement Monsters of Ohio by John Scalzi Sci-fi legend John Scalzi’s latest speculative adventure has a Lovecraftian tinge, as the locals in Richland, Ohio, take offence to the actions of a predatory private-equity firm – and develop some unexpected tentacles. The local police chief, and former resident Mike, get entangled in what’s going on and in events that are likely to change humanity forever. The Falling by Carole Hailey I always appreciate a good “asteroid hitting Earth” story (my recent-ish reads include Larry Niven and Jerry Pournelle’s Lucifer’s Hammer, a classic from 1977, and Not With A Bang by Temi Oh, a twist on the tale). Carole Hailey’s previous book, The Silence Project, was great, so I’m looking forward to her take on this story. It follows Cassie, who grew up with a father obsessed with an impending apocalypse. Now she’s middle-aged and discovers that his teachings might have some use after all when an asteroid is found in the solar system, heading for northern Europe. Michael Moorcock, who has a new book out this month Ulf Andersen/Getty Images The Wounds of Albion by Michael Moorcock There aren’t many names in science fiction and fantasy bigger than Michael Moorcock, and this is the final part of his “fictional autobiography”. It sees, if I understand the blurb correctly, the author tell the story of both his real life (from the impact of his science fiction to the music of the sixties) and of a fantasy world only he can see (the example given: “the Carmelite Monks must protect their latest multiverse-spanning invention”). Intriguingly weird, as you’d expect from this wonderful writer – I’m keen to see how, as we’re promised, “Moorcock meets ‘Moorcock’ and together they produce a remedy for the world’s pain!”. Cold Eternity by SA Barnes If I were SA Barnes, I would be pretty pleased with the moniker laid on me by my publisher: she is, apparently, “the queen of space horror”. In this latest, Halley Zwick (who is on the run) boards the spaceship Elysian Fields. This was sold to the super-rich as a place to enter cryo-sleep until their immortality could be assured, but it has been silent and dark for decades… although is it really? Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter On the Calculation of Volume V by Solvej Balle, translated by Jennifer Russell and Sophia Hersi Smith My colleague Gerardo loved previous instalments in this series, which follows a protagonist living the same day on repeat. Tara has now spent 12 years reliving 18 November, while her partner Thomas, to whom she has returned, repeats his own identical day. Tara sets off with her friends for a community where other time-stranded people have come together and begins to see a life beyond Thomas on the horizon. Bridge Planet Nine by Jared Throne This is a graphic novel in which four thieves travel to an abandoned colony planet (Bridge Planet Nine) with plans to rob one of the uncrewed freighter ships that land there. But it turns out this apparently deserted outpost isn’t as empty as they thought… Alfa by Lilja Sigurdardóttir, translated by Larissa Kyzer This speculative crime novel was shortlisted for the Icelandic Crime Book of the Year award. It’s set in Reykjavík in 2052, where an artificial intelligence manages society and ensures it is almost crime-free. Sabína discovers that her brother, a dissident who lives outside the controlling AI’s reach, has been murdered, and she begins investigating his final days. I’ve enjoyed Sigurdardóttir’s straight crime novels, so will definitely be exploring this one. Eternity’s Tomb by Dan Moren Ex-con Z is asked to help locate the tomb of Ikanto, which is hurtling through space towards a black hole. It’s a strange job offer – especially when it’s made by a floating brain in a jar. But Z is desperate and up for the challenge. This is an irreverent sort of caper, according to its publisher, and comparable to Guardians of the Galaxy – no bad thing in my eyes. Deadlock by Chloe Gong Humans have moved to virtual reality to escape a world that is falling apart, in the second dystopian novel in The Strangeloom Trilogy. We follow those working against megacorporation NileCorp to bring it down. Sounds like some cyberpunky, futuristic fun. When you make a purchase via the links on this page, we receive a commission.
summary: Top New Science-Fiction Books Released in November 2026.

title: Scientists find hidden cholesterol driver and block it, cutting LDL in mice
content: Scientists have identified a hidden mechanism by which high‑cholesterol diets can override the body’s natural cholesterol defenses, and they showed that blocking this mechanism dramatically reduced harmful LDL cholesterol in mice. An experimental drug that targets the pathway has already cleared an early‑stage human safety trial, opening the possibility of faster development of a new cholesterol treatment.
summary: Scientists uncovered a hidden mechanism by which high‑cholesterol diets undermine the body's natural cholesterol defenses and showed that blocking it dramatically lowered LDL cholesterol in mice. An experimental drug targeting this pathway has already passed an early human safety trial, potentially accelerating development of a new high‑cholesterol treatment.

title: Scientists find trees use specialized wood like opposing muscles to straighten trunks
content: Scientists have found that trees are able to sense their own shape and straighten their trunks by using specialized wood that functions like opposing muscles. This self‑correcting mechanism helps trees maintain posture and, according to the researchers, may contribute to stronger forests, improved timber quality and more resilient crops.
summary: Scientists have discovered that trees can sense their own shape and straighten their trunks using specialized wood that acts like opposing muscles. This ability helps trees maintain posture and could lead to stronger forests, better timber, and more resilient crops.
author: Science Daily

title: Forgotten neutrino may explain matter survival after Big Bang, say scientists
content: Scientists say a long‑overlooked neutrino could explain why matter survived the Big Bang, making stars, planets and life possible. They argue the particle reshaped the early universe and may have produced gravitational‑wave signals that are potentially detectable, offering a new way to probe fundamental cosmic mysteries.
summary: Scientists say a mysterious particle that has been overlooked for decades could explain why matter survived the Big Bang, enabling stars, planets and life. They suggest the forgotten neutrino reshaped the early universe and may have produced detectable gravitational‑wave signals.

content: Hundreds of adult gaming centres in England have bingo licences that still qualify them for discounted business rates Hundreds of high street “ slot farms ” could continue claiming a discount on their business rates, unless the government closes a loophole that allows them to pose as bingo halls. content:

title: UK children’s minister Josh MacAlister visits Denmark to study top children’s homes
content:
UK children’s minister Josh MacAlister has travelled to Copenhagen to examine the Danish residential‑care model. His visit follows concerns that England’s children’s‑home system is in crisis, prompting the British government to look abroad for possible solutions.

In a quiet suburb on the outskirts of Copenhagen, MacAlister inspected Josephine Schneider’s House, a large white building set back from the road behind a plum tree with purple leaves. The house blends in with neighboring properties and bears little outward signage, yet it is described as one of the best children’s homes in the world.

Danish children’s homes are frequently cited as the global gold standard of residential care. The British government is studying these Danish facilities as part of its effort to develop a roadmap to address the challenges facing England’s own children’s‑home system.
summary: UK children’s minister Josh MacAlister travelled to Copenhagen to examine Denmark’s residential care model, including the highly regarded Josephine Schneider’s House. The British government is studying Danish children’s homes as a possible roadmap to address the crisis in England’s own children’s home system.

title: Rachel Reeves says UK should rejoin EU, backs Andy Burnham on Brexit
content: Former chancellor says leaving European Union has made Britain ‘poorer, weaker and less secure’ The former chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK’s future should be inside the EU, saying Brexit has made the UK “poorer, weaker and less secure”. title: Binance recovers 90% of $6.3bn hack losses; FBI attributes attack to North Korean group
content: Cryptocurrency exchange says withdrawals starting to resume on Sunday as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced 90% of the ⁠amount stolen after a record $6.3bn hack of its platform by a group the FBI identified as being backed by North Korea. title: Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream as Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
content: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! content:

content:

summary: Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez won a unanimous decision over Christian Mbilli to regain the WBC super‑middleweight title in Riyadh. title: Maresca blames “silly” errors after City lose to Brighton 1-0
content: Matheus Nunes mistake lets in Yasin Ayari for winner Maresca: ‘We are conceding silly goals that we can avoid’ Enzo Maresca said “silly goals” and individual errors are costing Manchester City after Matheus Nunes’ mistake allowed Yasin Ayari to score Brighton’s winner in Saturday’s 1-0 victory here. title: Lewis Hamilton takes first Ferrari pole at Mexican Grand Prix, Antonelli fourth
content: George Russell second on grid after qualifying Antonelli well placed as he nears title confirmation Even as Formula One’s young gun Kimi Antonelli remains on course to claim his first world championship on Sunday it was the veteran, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton who gave a salutary reminder that there is very much fight left in the old dog yet as he claimed a spectacular pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix. Hamilton delivered a superb lap for Ferrari to secure his first pole for the team and just beat Mercedes’ George Russell into second. World champion in waiting Antonelli was in fourth place but remains in position to close out the title on Sunday, although Hamilton and Russell, who must win the race to have any hope of keeping the fight alive, have at least locked out the front row.

title: Kane misses penalty as Bayern Munich draws 2-2 with Dortmund
content:
Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund drew 2-2 in Der Klassiker on Saturday, a result that left the two teams level on points at the top of the league. The match featured a late equalizer from Borussia Dortmund’s Fabio Silva, who scored in the final moments to secure the share of spoils for his side.

Harry Kane, the recent Ballon d’Or winner, started the match for Bayern Munich but missed a penalty kick while his team led 1-0. Kane had been an unused substitute during Bayern’s 6-1 German Cup victory over Magdeburg on Wednesday but returned to the starting lineup for the league fixture.

In addition to the missed penalty, Kane struck the post during the encounter. The incident was one of four times Bayern Munich hit the woodwork in the game.
summary: Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post as Bayern Munich drew 2-2 with Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker. A last-gasp equaliser by Fabio Silva kept the teams level on points at the top of the league.

content:

After a low-quality first half where Rangers managed only one shot on target, Aberdeen’s manager Derek McInnes’s side increased their pace in the second half.

Despite surviving sustained pressure from the visitors, Aberdeen conceded in the 83rd minute when Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net. The goal marked Naderi’s eighth of the season, breaking down the home side’s stubborn resistance to seal the win.
summary: Ryan Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice in the 83rd minute to score Rangers’ only goal in a 1-0 win over Aberdeen at Hampden Park. The victory secures Rangers a place in the Premier Sports Cup final.

title: Jonathan Wilson: Mikel Arteta's "dossier" strategy is dangerous for Arsenal
content: The manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories have reached new levels English football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today as Mikel Arteta collates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area. Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. During Arsenal’s 2-0 win against Everton last Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.”
summary: Mikel Arteta collected images of rival managers leaving their technical areas after receiving his second booking for doing so. Jonathan Wilson argues that this approach, which Arteta defends as a counter to perceived bias, is a dangerous tactic for the club.

title: Alex Mitchell limps off with hamstring as Northampton beat Gloucester 28-14
content:
Northampton secured a 28-14 victory over Gloucester, a result that underscores the team’s defensive resilience against early-season pace-setters. The match highlighted the absence of England scrum-half Alex Mitchell, who limped off with a suspected hamstring pull, adding to the national team’s injury concerns ahead of next Sunday’s autumn opener against Australia. Despite the setback, Northampton weathered the loss to score 28 unanswered points after withstanding Gloucester’s early onslaught.

The performance marked a stark contrast to Northampton’s previous league outing, where 119 points were scored. This victory was built on strong defensive efforts, with Tom Pearson, who is back in the England picture this autumn, delivering an outstanding display throughout the game.
summary: Alex Mitchell left the match with a suspected hamstring pull, making his participation in England’s upcoming autumn opener against Australia uncertain. Despite his exit, Northampton held off Gloucester to win 28‑14, scoring 28 unanswered points.

title: Carrick to lead Manchester United against Roma after Chelsea defeat
content:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has confirmed he will remain in charge for the upcoming Champions League match against Roma on Tuesday. This assurance comes despite the team’s 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday, which extended United’s winless streak to nine games. Carrick is currently navigating a difficult period, as the club has endured its longest such run since 1988.

During his post-match analysis, Carrick focused on defensive errors, specifically highlighting the moment Morgan Rogers scored for Chelsea. Rogers broke through the center of United’s defense, a goal Carrick described as a significant turning point when the match was balanced. While acknowledging the severity of conceding in that manner, Carrick stated he is now concentrating on preparing his players for the midweek fixture.
summary: Michael Carrick stated he will remain in charge for Manchester United's upcoming Champions League match against Roma. The manager made this declaration after a 2-0 loss to Chelsea extended the club's winless run to nine games.

title: Nighttime bat surveys aid science and reshape public perception
content:
People often react with curiosity when they hear a chirping sound on a detector or feel something whiz past, moments that signal an encounter with microbats. The title notes that seeking these animals after dark can aid scientific research and shift public perception of the creatures.

Microbats are described as small, primarily nocturnal mammals that navigate and hunt using ultrasonic echolocation. They emit calls and listen to the returning echoes to locate objects and prey.
summary: Researchers conduct after‑dark searches for microbats, which are small nocturnal mammals that navigate and hunt using ultrasonic echolocation. The resulting data can advance scientific knowledge and change how people view these animals.

title: NES Contra 1987 ported from assembly to C and WebAssembly with online co‑op
content:
A Show HN post announces a browser‑based port of the 1987 NES game Contra. The author used vermiceli’s annotated disassembly of the original ROM as a reference, translating the 6502 assembly routine by routine into C and verifying each frame against the original using the Mesen emulator. The resulting C code was then compiled to WebAssembly, allowing the game to run in a web browser.

The port adds online multiplayer, enabling two players to cooperate over the internet. The project’s source code is hosted on GitHub, and the submission has received 28 points and 17 comments on Hacker News.
summary: The 1987 NES game Contra was translated routine‑by‑routine from its 6502 assembly into C and then compiled to WebAssembly to run in a browser. The port adds online multiplayer so two players can play co‑op over the internet.

title: Boot Sector Language Model Generates Infinite Linux Boot Logs
content:
A new language model project has been showcased on Hacker News, featuring an inference engine that fits entirely within a 510-byte Master Boot Record (MBR). The project draws inspiration from the boot sector demo scene, where developers previously created applications such as chess games and C compilers in 512 bytes. This neural network generates Linux boot logs for non-existent hardware by producing dmesg messages infinitely. The system utilizes a small character-level network trained on dmesg data, with the weights, vocabulary, and strings stored in the sectors immediately following the MBR.

During development, the creator identified a specific bug by comparing the output of a Python simulator with the assembly code running in QEMU. Although the initial characters matched, the output eventually diverged. By retrieving hidden layer values via QEMU’s debug port, it was determined that only the first neuron was calculated correctly. The issue stemmed from the idiv instruction, which stores its remainder in the edx register, overwriting the pointer to the biases table. This caused the first neuron to be biased correctly while subsequent neurons used garbage data. The fix involved determining the bias address from the loop counter to ensure no pointers survived the division operation.

A second bug was discovered by inspecting the code before the initial run. The BIOS print routine zeros out the bx register, which contained the predicted character number. This necessitated the use of push and pop instructions to preserve the value of bx around the print call. The project contrasts with Sectorllm, which runs a 5-layer Llama2 model with an attention mechanism in 1.2K of assembly code. In contrast, this project prioritizes fitting the engine into a single sector, resulting in a network with just one hidden layer of int8 operations.
summary: A 510‑byte MBR contains an inference engine that uses a small char‑level neural network to generate Linux boot messages infinitely. The author debugged integer‑arithmetic bugs, fixing bias pointer and BIOS print routine issues to match QEMU output.

title: Government corruption tops concerns of US midterm voters, poll shows
content:
A recent exclusive poll indicates that government corruption has emerged as a top issue for voters heading into the US midterm elections. The article highlights that alleged self-dealing by the president and his allies is becoming a significant concern for the electorate. This shift in voter sentiment contrasts with historical political narratives, such as the “welfare queen” trope popularized by Ronald Reagan in 1976, which focused on fraud by the poor rather than high-level governmental misconduct.

The text details several specific allegations of financial entanglements involving the Trump administration and its associates. It notes that the Qatari government gifted the president a luxury jet, a move that potentially violates the emoluments clause of the constitution. Additionally, the UAE reportedly gained access to high-end American AI chips shortly after an investment firm linked to its ruling family purchased a $500 million stake in World Liberty Financial, a crypto company funded by the families of Trump and Steve Witkoff.

Further examples of alleged self-dealing include the pardons granted to Wanda Vázquez Garced, the former governor of Puerto Rico, and Julio Herrera Velutini, a banker who paid her bribes. These pardons followed a $50 million deal between Velutini’s family and Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, as well as a $3.5 million donation to Trump’s Maga Inc Super Pac. The article also points to the Pentagon lending over $600 million to Vulcan Elements, a rare earths startup, three months after Donald Jr’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, acquired a stake in the company.

Finally, the piece mentions Powerus, a drone maker backed by Eric and Donald Trump, which is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies. The source characterizes this as enriching the president’s children from a war launched without consulting Congress. These incidents collectively form the basis for the growing voter concern regarding corruption in the government.
summary: An exclusive poll found that government corruption is a top issue for US midterm voters. The report cites alleged self‑dealing by President Trump and his allies, including a Qatari‑gifted luxury jet, UAE access to American AI chips after a stake purchase, and donations linked to pardons.

title: Police clash with masked rioters in Paris and Marseille after large French protests
content:
Clashes erupted in Paris, Marseille, and other French cities following a third wave of protests concerning the cost of living and deteriorating public services. According to the interior ministry, approximately 320,000 people participated in rallies nationwide, a decrease from the estimated 410,000 attendees the previous weekend. In Paris, 70,000 demonstrators, some wearing Halloween costumes, marched along boulevards on the south-eastern outskirts, deliberately avoiding the city centre.

Simultaneous demonstrations occurred in Germany, where police deployed teargas to disperse crowds as evening approached. The French protests marked the third consecutive weekend of unrest, with masked rioters engaging in clashes with police forces in several major cities.
summary: Police clash with masked rioters in Paris and Marseille after large French protests.

title: Oleshky evacuees reunite with families after truce permits crossing into Ukraine
content:
Evacuees from the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory on Saturday and were reunited with their families. The crossing occurred under a truce described as the most significant since Russia’s full‑scale invasion began four and a half years ago, and the major rescue operation that enabled it started on Friday.

Residents of nearby villages lined the highway, waving flags to greet the convoy as it entered the area. The operation facilitated the movement of the Oleshky evacuees across the front line during the brief cease‑fire.
summary: Evacuees from the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory on Saturday and were reunited with their families. The major rescue operation began on Friday and was carried out under the most significant truce since Russia’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine four and a half years ago.
